---
title: Webhooks
description: Signed response.submitted delivery, with retries and a dead-letter queue.
---

Per-form webhook endpoints receive a signed `response.submitted` event on submission. That is the
only event type: there is no form-published, session-started or response-erased event.

## The request

```json
{
  "eventId": "a1b2c3d4",
  "eventType": "response.submitted",
  "deliveredAt": "2026-07-20T02:05:00.000Z",
  "payload": {
    "sessionId": "ses_",
    "formId": "frm_",
    "formVersion": 3,
    "submittedAt": "2026-07-20T02:04:59.000Z",
    "contentHash": "",
    "answers": [{ "questionId": "q_name", "value": "Ada" }]
  }
}
```

`answers` is an array of entries rather than an object keyed by question, because one question can
be answered more than once. Order is meaning: document order for questions, roster order for
instances. Inside a repeating group each entry also carries an `instanceId`, and that key is absent
for every question outside a group. Nothing about repetition sits outside `answers`: there is no
groups member, no rows, no instances and no instance count anywhere in the envelope.

| Header              | Value                                                    |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `X-QCMS-Event`      | the event type                                            |
| `X-QCMS-Delivery`   | a fresh UUID, unique per attempt; a retry has a new one   |
| `X-QCMS-Timestamp`  | Unix seconds when the request was signed                  |
| `X-QCMS-Signature`  | `v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, timestamp + "." + body)>`    |

## Verifying

Recompute the HMAC over the timestamp, a dot, and the raw body bytes, with your webhook secret, and
compare it in constant time to the hex after `v1=`. Verify against the raw request bytes, before any
JSON re-serialization. Reject if the timestamp is too old, for example more than five minutes, to
bound replay. Because the timestamp is signed, a consumer that checks its freshness gets replay
protection.

## Retries

A delivery succeeds on any `2xx` within the timeout. Anything else, including a non-2xx, a timeout,
a network error or a delivery-time URL rejection, is a failed attempt. The delivery is rescheduled
with capped exponential backoff, one minute, then five, then twenty-five, capped at six hours, and
after ten failed attempts it is dead-lettered.

The recorded error is a value-free code, never a secret or an answer value. The attempt counter
counts failed attempts, so a delivery that succeeded first time reads zero.

Delivery is at least once, so a consumer can receive a duplicate. `eventId` is stable per outbox
event and `contentHash` is stable per submission; both are idempotency keys, and processing the same
event id twice must be a no-op.

## Configuring an endpoint

| Route                                       | Effect                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `POST /admin/forms/:id/webhooks`            | Configure a webhook. The secret is generated if omitted, and shown exactly once in the response |
| `GET /admin/forms/:id/webhooks`             | List the form's webhooks. Secrets are masked and never returned                                |
| `PUT /admin/forms/:id/webhooks/:webhookId`  | Update the URL or active flag, or rotate the secret; the new secret is shown once               |
| `DELETE /admin/forms/:id/webhooks/:webhookId` | Soft-deactivate, so delivery history survives                                                |

Multiple webhooks per form are allowed, and delivery goes to every active one.

Endpoints are per environment: configuration is authored once per environment, and a promotion does
not carry it.

Rotating a secret is a hard cutover. A delivery carries one signature under one secret, so there is
no overlap window and every delivery to that endpoint fails at the consumer until the consumer is
updated.

## Endpoint URL policy

By default the policy is deny. The scheme must be `https`, and the host must not be a loopback name
or an IP literal in a private, reserved, loopback or link-local range, in either IPv4 or IPv6. A
rejected URL answers `422 WEBHOOK_URL_REJECTED` with a reason. The check runs at configuration time
and again immediately before every delivery.

`QCMS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true` is the single documented escape hatch. Note honestly that the
guard does not fully close DNS rebinding: a hostname that passed can resolve to a private address at
fetch time.

:::caution[No credentials in the URL]
Do not put a bearer token in a query parameter, an API key in the path, or basic-auth credentials in
the host. The secret and the signature are the authentication.
:::

## Two-person rule

A workspace carries one switch for requiring a second approver, off by default. With it on, the
three configuring routes answer `202` in production instead of applying the change, and the body
marks the change pending. A `202` is neither an error nor a success. A create still answers with the
secret. One pending change per endpoint: a second proposal for the same endpoint is refused.

## Operations

`GET /admin/outbox/dead-letters` lists dead letters deployment-wide, newest first.
`POST /admin/forms/:id/deliveries/:deliveryId/redeliver` retries one.
`GET /admin/forms/:id/deliveries` lists recent deliveries. There is no bulk-redelivery route.

In the admin, per-form webhook configuration and the delivery dashboard live on the form's Webhooks
tab, and the dead-letter queue has its own screen.

## Configuration

`QCMS_APP_KEY`, `QCMS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE` (default `false`), `QCMS_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` (default
`10000`), `QCMS_WEBHOOK_BATCH_SIZE` (default `20`), `QCMS_OUTBOX_INTERVAL_MS` and
`QCMS_OUTBOX_JITTER_MS`.

Secrets are encrypted at rest rather than hashed, with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from
`QCMS_APP_KEY`.
